segments.text: How long do you actually need to be in the sauna to get the benefits? These are the three tiers of sauna and each one triggers a different set of benefits for your body. Tier one, this is the bare minimum. It's linked to increased life expectancy and chronic disease prevention in population studies, but you're still not getting cellular repair. Tier two, this is the sweet spot. Studies show four to seven times per week at this range is linked to reductions in mortality, heart disease, and dementia risk. After doing over 200 sessions of this dose, here's what we saw in my body. A 10-year reduction in

vascular age, 87% reduction in microplastics in my blood, and complete elimination in my semen, and a measurable reduction of environmental toxins. This is the tier I'd recommend to almost anyone, but there's more. Tier three, this is the deep repair tier and it doesn't happen at a fixed time. It happens when your core body temperature crosses roughly 102.2° F. This triggers the release of heat shock proteins, a cellular repair crew that fixes damaged proteins before they clump together. For me, this takes 31 minutes at 200° F, but [music] everyone's number is different.

Friends, these are recommendations I built based off of scientific research and things I've personally tested on my body. If you want one protocol, aim for 20 minutes or more at 200° F four to seven times per week. And men, don't forget ice your balls.
